correctness.rationale: Differentiating F gives F’=G/[2sqrt(z)(1-dz^4)^2], with G correct; h_j derivatives strictly positive for 0<z<=1/3, so no earlier root. Reconstructed Q(v)=(1+v)^8 G(v/(1+v)): all 9 coefficients independently computed with SymPy, B0-B2>0, B7-B8<0; the exact inequality B4-(26/7)B3=-9+7d-648a/7-318b/7<-2 excludes the only potential 5-sign-change pattern. Descartes gives at most 3 positive roots counted with multiplicity; endpoint derivative signs imply an odd total, hence 1 or 3. Exact-rational independent substitutions at z=1/2,3/5,3/4,9/10 give +,-,+,-, forcing 3 distinct simple roots and exactly 2 local maxima. This is a universal algebraic proof, not extrapolation of the witness.
